facts.statement: Trilophosuchus is an extinct genus of mekosuchine crocodilian that lived in Australia.
facts.quote: Trilophosuchus ("triple crest crocodile") is an extinct genus of mekosuchine crocodilian from Australia.

facts.statement: Fossils of Trilophosuchus have been found at the Ringtail Site in north-western Queensland, dating to the Miocene epoch.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found at the Ringtail Site in the Riversleigh World Heritage Area (north-western Queensland) and date to the Miocene epoch.

facts.statement: Additional remains found at the older Hiatus Site extend the known range of Trilophosuchus into the Oligocene.
facts.quote: Additional remains have also been found at the older Hiatus Site and extend its range into the Oligocene.

facts.statement: Trilophosuchus is thought to have had a short, blunt snout and large eyes, resembling modern dwarf crocodiles.
facts.quote: Like the closely related Mekosuchus, it is thought to have had a short and blunt snout and large eyes that generally resembles today's dwarf crocodiles.

facts.statement: The holotype skull was uncovered in 1985 and is considered one of the best-preserved fossil crocodilians from Australia despite missing the snout.
facts.quote: The holotype skull was uncovered in 1985 during an excavation by the University of New South Wales and is currently considered to be among the best preserved fossil crocodilians from Australia, in spite of the missing snout.

facts.statement: The genus Trilophosuchus was erected in 1993 by Paul Willis of the University of New South Wales.
facts.quote: The genus Trilophosuchus was erected in 1993 with the description of the remains by Paul Willis of the University of New South Wales in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.

facts.statement: The name Trilophosuchus translates to "triple-crested crocodile" and refers to three parallel ridges running along the skull table.
facts.quote: The name Trilophosuchus derives from Ancient Greek and translates to "triple-crested crocodile", referring to the three parallel ridges that run along the animal's skull table.

facts.statement: The species name rackhami honors Alan Rackham Senior, a supporter of the Riversleigh excavations.
facts.quote: The species name meanwhile honors Alan Rackham Senior, a supporter of the excavations in the Riversleigh WHA.

facts.statement: The snout of Trilophosuchus is thought to have been very robust with a trapezoid cross-section just before the eyes.
facts.quote: The snout, though incomplete, is thought to have been very robust, showcasing a trapezoid cross-section just before the eyes.

facts.statement: The most distinct feature of Trilophosuchus is the presence of three prominent crests extending along the skull table.
facts.quote: The most distinct feature of Trilophosuchus, and the one that gives this taxon its name, is the presence of three prominent crests that extend alongside the length of the crocodilian's skull table.

facts.statement: The central crest originates between the eyes on the frontal bone and continues onto the parietal bone, ending near the supratemporal fenestrae.
facts.quote: The central crest originates on the broad frontal bone between the eyes and continues onto the parietal bone before ending approximately at the same level as the supratemporal fenestrae.

facts.statement: Two additional crests run parallel to the central ridge, originating at the orbital margin and extending to the end of the skull table.
facts.quote: Two additional crests run parallel to this medial ridge, originating at the orbital margin and stretching from there until the end of the skull table, occupying the space between the midline and the fenestrae.

facts.statement: The precise number of teeth in Trilophosuchus is currently unknown because no specimen preserves the front of the skull.
facts.quote: As no specimen of Trilophosuchus preserves the front of the skull, the precise number of teeth is currently unknown.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the Oligocene material found at the Hiatus Site represents a second species of Trilophosuchus or simply age-related variation.
facts.quote: One referred specimen, a parietal, has been collected the older Hiatus Site, putting the oldest appearance of the genus within the Oligocene. This Oligocene material differs subtly and may represent a second species or could simply be the result of age or intraspecific variation.

facts.statement: Only a single species, T. rackhami, has been described for the genus Trilophosuchus.
facts.quote: Only a single species has been described, the type species T. rackhami.

facts.statement: Trilophosuchus possesses a unique acute dural peak above the hindbrain, a feature shared only with Agaresuchus and Arenysuchus among eusuchians.
facts.quote: One of the most unique features of Trilophosuchus is the presence of an acute dural peak, an inflation above the hindbrain.

facts.statement: The inner ear of Trilophosuchus has a sub-triangular vestibular apparatus, unlike the rounded shape found in most modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: The inner ear features a distinctly sub-triangular vestibular apparatus (where the semicircular canals contact the common crus), as opposed to being more rounded like in other modern crocodilians.

facts.statement: The skull of Trilophosuchus measures only 79 mm from the back of the head to the front of the rostrum, indicating a very small size.
facts.quote: The skull of Trilophosuchus only measures 79 mm from the back of the head to the front most preserved part of the rostrum, making it very small even when accounting for the missing material.

facts.statement: Evidence of skull bone fusion and surface sculpting indicates that the holotype specimen of Trilophosuchus was an adult when it died.
facts.quote: Both the fusion of the skull bones and the sculpting on their surface indicate that it was in fact an adult at the time of its death.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Trilophosuchus was a dwarf species exhibiting juvenile-like traits due to paedomorphy rather than being an immature individual.
facts.quote: This would suggest that rather than being immature, Trilophosuchus was simply a dwarf species, with the juvenile characteristics being the result of paedomorphy.

facts.statement: Despite resembling early crocodyliforms, Trilophosuchus is classified as an advanced crocodylian.
facts.quote: Despite its superficial resemblance to early crocodyliforms such as protosuchians and notosuchians, Trilophosuchus is an advanced crocodylian.

facts.statement: Trilophosuchus belongs to the subfamily Mekosuchinae, a group of endemic Australian and New Caledonian crocodiles.
facts.quote: Eventually dubbed Mekosuchinae following the inclusion of Mekosuchus from New Caledonia and Australia.

facts.statement: A 2018 study by Stein et al. placed Trilophosuchus as a basal form related to Ultrastenos, a result later deemed irregular due to problematic taxa.
facts.quote: One outlier to this is the phylogenetic tree recovered by Stein et al. (2018), which recovered it as a more basal form related to Ultrastenos.

facts.statement: Trilophosuchus was an extinct crocodilian genus belonging to the subfamily Mekosuchinae.
facts.quote: Trilophosuchus ("cocodrilo de tres crestas") es un género extinto de crocodiliano de la subfamilia Mekosuchinae.

facts.statement: Trilophosuchus measured approximately 1.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Trilophosuchus medía aproximadamente 1.5 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Trilophosuchus had a short skull with three ridges on the top and large eyes.
facts.quote: Tenía un cráneo corto con tres bordes en la parte superior y ojos grandes.

facts.statement: The skull of Trilophosuchus was discovered in 1985 during an excavation by the University of New South Wales.
facts.quote: El cráneo fue descubierto en 1985 durante una excavación realizada por la Universidad de Nueva Gales del Sur.

facts.statement: The genus Trilophosuchus was named in 1993 by Paul Willis of the University of Sydney in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.
facts.quote: El género Trilophosuchus fue denominado en 1993 con la descripción de los restos por Paul Willis de la Universidad de Sídney en la publicación Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.

facts.statement: Trilophosuchus lived in the early Miocene, approximately 20 million years ago.
facts.quote: El depósito en el cual se halló a Trilophosaurus es de principios del Mioceno, hace más o menos 20 millones de años.

facts.statement: The fossil range of Trilophosuchus spans from the Early to Middle Miocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Mioceno Inferior-Medio

facts.statement: The authority for the genus Trilophosuchus is Willis, 1993.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Willis, 1993

facts.statement: The type species of Trilophosuchus is T. rackhami, described by Willis in 1993.
facts.quote: subdivision: T. rackhami Willis, 1993 (especie tipo)

facts.statement: Researchers propose that Trilophosuchus was restricted to small prey, analogous to small agamas and iguanas, fitting its small body size compared to larger terrestrial crocodylomorphs.
facts.quote: Willis proposes that the difference between these large terrestrial crocodylomorphs and Trilophosuchus may be analogues to the differences between large monitor lizards like the Komodo dragon and small agamas and iguanas. This would suggest that Trilophosuchus was restricted to small prey, fitting its small body size.

facts.statement: It is unclear how Trilophosuchus and Mekosuchus sanderi differed in their ecology despite both being thought to be terrestrial animals.
facts.quote: It is thus unclear how the two would have differed in their ecology.

facts.statement: The Ringtail Site where Trilophosuchus fossils were found preserves evidence of a pool in a forested karst terrain that included aquatic animals like lungfish, turtles, and the extinct platypus Obdurodon dicksoni.
facts.quote: The Ringtail Site is currently interpreted as a preserving what was once a pool located in a forested karst terrain, preserving primarily aquatic animals that, aside from the crocodilians, includes lungfish, chelid turtles and the extinct platypus Obdurodon dicksoni.

facts.statement: Trilophosuchus had a short, high skull with relatively large eyes.
facts.quote: Trilophosuchus tenía un cráneo corto y alto con ojos relativamente grandes.

facts.statement: Although only the skull is known, Trilophosuchus is estimated to have been about 1.5 meters long.
facts.quote: Aunque solo se conoce el cráneo, se estima que Trilophosuchus mediría alrededor de 1.5 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Trilophosuchus resembles some primitive crocodiliforms such as notosuchians, atoposaurids, and protosuchians.
facts.quote: También se parece a algunos crocodiliformes primitivos como los notosuquios, atoposáuridos y protosuquios.

facts.statement: As a mekosuchine, Trilophosuchus was not closely related to those groups and likely acquired its short snout and small body size through convergent evolution.
facts.quote: Siendo un mekosuquino, Trilophosuchus no estaba cercanamente a ninguno de esos grupos y probablemente adquirió su hocico corto y el pequeño tamaño corporal a través de la evolución convergente.

facts.statement: The posterior surface of the skull had structures for muscle insertion that may have allowed it to hold its head above the body.
facts.quote: El occipital o superficie posterior del cráneo tenía estructuras para la inserción de los músculos que le pudieron haber permitido sostener la cabeza sobre el cuerpo.

facts.statement: Trilophosuchus is an advanced crocodilian.
facts.quote: Trilophosuchus es un crocodiliano avanzado.

facts.statement: Trilophosuchus was initially considered the most basal known mekosuchine.
facts.quote: Trilophosuchus fue inicialmente considerado como el más basal de los mekosuquinos conocidos.

facts.statement: Later phylogenetic studies placed Trilophosuchus as a more derived mekosuchine, more closely related to recent forms like Quinkana and Mekosuchus.
facts.quote: Estudios filogenéticos posteriores han situado a Trilophosuchus como un mekosuquino más derivado, más cercanamente relacionado con formas recientes como Quinkana y Mekosuchus.

facts.statement: These forms are placed in the derived mekosuchine clade Mekosuchini to distinguish them from more basal taxa like Kambara and Australosuchus.
facts.quote: Estos han sido situados en el clado derivado mekosquino Mekosuchini para distinguirlo de los taxones más basales como Kambara y Australosuchus.

facts.statement: Trilophosuchus lived from the Chattian to the Serravallian, between 27.3 and 11.63 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Chattian to Serravallian (27.3 to 11.63 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species of Trilophosuchus is Trilophosuchus rackhami.
facts.quote: Type species: Trilophosuchus rackhami

facts.statement: Trilophosuchus is unusual among mekosuchines and crocodilians in general for having a short, high snout and an arboreal lifestyle.
facts.quote: Trilophosuchus es inusual entre los mekosuquinos, y los crocodilianos en general, ya que tenía un hocico corto y alto y un estilo de vida arborícola.

facts.statement: These primitive mekosuchines were terrestrial, unlike their relatives, the semiaquatic crocodiles.
facts.quote: Todos estos mekosuquinos primitivos eran terrestres, a diferencia de sus parientes, los cocodrilos semiacuáticos.

facts.statement: The short snout contrasts with the long snouts of large carnivorous crocodilians like Pristichampsus, suggesting Trilophosuchus restricted its diet to small prey.
facts.quote: La corta longitud del hocico, contrasta con los hocicos largos de los grandes crocodilianos carnívoros como Pristichampsus, lo que sugiere que Trilophosaurus restringía su dieta a presas pequeñas.

facts.statement: It may have consumed fish, turtles, snakes, and small mammals, all of which have been found at Riversleigh.
facts.quote: Puede haber consumido peces, tortugas, serpientes y mamíferos pequeños, todos los cuales han sido hallados en Riversleigh.

facts.statement: Because Trilophosuchus is similar in appearance to M. inexpectatus, it has frequently been suggested that it was also arboreal.
facts.quote: Dado que Trilophosuchus es similar en apariencia a M. inexpectatus, se ha sugerido frecuentemente que también era arbóreo.

facts.statement: Mekosuchus inexpectatus had limb bone structures compatible with climbing, but there is no evidence that Trilophosuchus had climbing abilities.
facts.quote: Mekosuchus inexpectatus tenía una estructura de los huesos de sus miembros que puede ser compatible con la capacidad de vivir en los árboles, pero no hay ninguna evidencia de que Trilophosuchus tuviera habilidades para trepar.

facts.statement: Due to a lack of evidence, there is no agreement among paleontologists regarding the lifestyle of this genus.
facts.quote: Debido a la carencia de evidencia, no hay acuerdo entre los paleontólogos sobre el estilo de vida de este género.
